summary:
[  edit  ]
The Noise  CHOP  makes an irregular wave that never repeats, with values approximately in the range -1 to +1.
It generates both smooth curves and noise that is random each sample. It uses the same math as the  Noise SOP .
You can create several curves with different shapes, and you can adjust period, amplitude, harmonics and more.
Optionally, an input can be connected. It is assumed that the input contains 1 to 3 channels representing X, Y and Z coordinates of points in space, and are used to sample anywhere in 3D noise space. One index in the input produces one sample in the output.
All noise functions work identically with  Time Slicing  on and off, with the exception of Harmonic Summation and Brownian whose methods cannot be limited to 1 in  Time Slice  mode. When the  Timeline  wraps around to frame 1, the noise functions will continue uninterrupted.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.name: type
parameters.description: ⊞  - The noise function used to generate noise. The functions available are:

parameters.label: Sparse
parameters.name: sparse
parameters.description: Produces high quality, continuous noise based on Sparse Convolution.

parameters.label: Hermite
parameters.name: hermite
parameters.description: Quicker than Sparse, but produces lower quality noise.

parameters.label: Harmomic Summation
parameters.name: harmonic
parameters.description: Sparse noise with the ability to control the frequency step of the harmonics. Slowest type.

parameters.label: Brownian
parameters.name: brownian
parameters.description: Works like a bug in random flight. With Num of Integrals at 2, its acceleration is changed randomly every frame.

parameters.label: Random
parameters.name: random
parameters.description: (White Noise) Every sample is random and unrelated to any other sample. It is the same as "white noise" in audio.

parameters.label: Alligator
parameters.name: alligator
parameters.description: Cell Noise.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Any number, integer or non-integer, which starts the random number generator. Each number gives completely different noise patterns, but with similar characteristics.

parameters.label: Period
parameters.name: period
parameters.description: The approximate separation between peaks of a noise cycle. It is expressed in Units. Increasing the period stretches the noise pattern out.

parameters.label: Period Unit
parameters.name: periodunit
parameters.description: Select the units to use for this parameter, Samples, Frames, Seconds, or Fraction.

parameters.label: Harmonics
parameters.name: harmon
parameters.description: The number of higher frequency components to layer on top of the base frequency. The higher this number, the bumpier the noise will be (as long as roughness is not set to zero). 0 harmonics give the base shape.

parameters.label: Harmonic Spread
parameters.name: spread
parameters.description: The factor by which the frequency of the harmonics are increased. It is normally 2. A spread of 3 and a base frequency of 0.1Hz will produce harmonics at 0.3Hz, 0.9Hz, 2.7Hz, etc. This parameter is only valid for the Harmonic Summation type.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.name: rough
parameters.description: Controls the effect of the higher frequency noise. When roughness is zero, all harmonics above the base frequency have no effect. At one, all harmonics are equal in amplitude to the base frequency. When roughness is between one and zero, the amplitude of higher harmonics drops off exponentially from the base frequency.

parameters.label: The default roughness is 0.5. This means the amplitude of the first harmonic is 0.5 of the base frequency, the second is 0.25, the third is 0.125. The harmonics are added to the base to give the final shape. The Harmonics parameter and the Roughness parameter must both be non
parameters.description: zero to see the harmonic effects.

parameters.label: Exponent
parameters.name: exp
parameters.description: Pushes the noise values toward 0, or +1 and -1. (It raises the value to the power of the exponent.) Exponents greater than one will pull the channel toward zero, and powers less than one will pull peaks towards +1 and -1. It is used to reshape the channels.

parameters.label: Num of Integrals
parameters.name: numint
parameters.description: Defines the number of times to integrate (see the Area  CHOP  p. 114) the Brownian noise. Higher values produce smoother curves with fewer features. Values beyond 4 produce somewhat identical curves. This parameter is only valid for the Random noise type.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.name: amp
parameters.description: Defines the noise value's amplitude (a scale on the values output).

parameters.label: Reset
parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: Only available if operator's   Time Slice   Parameter is on. Toggling this parameter will reset the noise calculation and hold the value until the parameter is released again.

parameters.label: Reset  Pulse
parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.description: Only available if operator's   Time Slice   Parameter is on. Pulsing this parameter will reset the noise calculation.

parameters.label: The Translate, Rotate, Scale and Pivot parameters let you sample in a different part of the 3D noise space. Imagine a different noise value for every XYZ point in space. Normally, the Noise  CHOP  samples the noise space from (0,0,0) along the X
parameters.description: axis in steps of 2/period.  /tx /ty /tz /rx /ry /rx /sx /sy /sz /px /py /pz

parameters.label: By changing the transform, you are translating, rotating and scaling the line along which the Noise CHOPs samples the noise space. A slight Y-rotation is like walking in a straight path in the mountains, recording your altitude along the way, then re-starting from the same initial location, walking in a slightly different direction. Your altitude starts off being similar but then diverges.    Transform Order
parameters.name: xord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Changing the Transform Order will change where things go much the same way as going a block and turning east gets you to a different place than turning east and then going a block. In matrix math terms, if we use the 'multiply vector on the right' (column vector) convention, a transform order of Scale, Rotate, Translate would be written as T * R * S * Position

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: rord
parameters.description: ⊞  - As with transform order (above), changing the order in which the rotations take place will alter the final position and orientation. A Rotation order of Rx Ry Rz would create the final rotation matrix as follows R = Rz * Ry * Rx

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.name: t
parameters.description: ⊞  - XYZ translation values.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: r
parameters.description: ⊞  - XYZ rotation, in degrees.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: s
parameters.description: ⊞  - XYZ scale to shrink or enlarge the transform.

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.name: p
parameters.description: ⊞  - XYZ pivot to apply the above operations around.

parameters.label: Constraint
parameters.name: constraint
parameters.description: ⊞  - Constraint and its parameters allows the noise curve to start and/or end at selected values. The mean value may also be enforced.  Note:  This only works when  Time Slice  is Off because time slicing has no pre-determined start/end.

parameters.label: None
parameters.name: none
parameters.description: No constraints set.

parameters.label: Start Value
parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Sets the noise starting position to the value set in 'Starting Value' parameter below.

parameters.label: End Value
parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Sets the noise ending position to the value set in 'Ending Value' parameter below.

parameters.label: Mean Value
parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Sets the noise mean position to the value set in the 'Mean Value' parameter below.

parameters.label: Start/End Values
parameters.name: endpoints
parameters.description: Set the starting and ending position of the noise separately using the parameters below.

parameters.label: Starting Value
parameters.name: constrstart
parameters.description: Value for the starting position.

parameters.label: Ending Value
parameters.name: constrend
parameters.description: Value for the ending position.

parameters.label: Mean Value
parameters.name: constrmean
parameters.description: Value for the mean value of the noise.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.name: normal
parameters.description: Ensures that all noise curves fall between -1 and 1. Applied before the Amplitude parameter. Only valid for Random and Harmonic Summation noise types, since Hermite and Sparse noise are always normalized. Normalizing random noise occurs between integrations, producing a more controlled curve.  Note:  This only works when  Time Slice  is Off because time slicing has no pre-determined start/end.

parameters.label: Channel Names
parameters.name: channelname
parameters.description: You can creates many channels with simple patterns like " chan[1-20] ", which generates 20 channels from chan1 to chan20. See the section, Common  CHOP  Parameters for a description of this and all Options. See  Scope and Channel Name Matching  Options. Each channel has a unique seed, so all channels will be different with the same parameter settings.
